tests/test_suite.c

The suite stops invalid implementations before ranking them. Literal cases check behavior, and an independent graph supplies small-string edit distances.

Check parser and normalization contracts at their boundaries

Section titled “Check parser and normalization contracts at their boundaries”

The parser table distinguishes missing equals signs, empty keys and valid empty values. Capacity cases test the exact limit and one byte over it. Normalization cases check separators, PascalCase/acronym tokens, unsupported punctuation and non-ASCII rejection.

Download complete source

Compare edit algorithms with shortest routes through a spelling graph

Section titled “Compare edit algorithms with shortest routes through a spelling graph”

Graph nodes are strings over abc up to length four. An edge represents one allowed edit. Breadth-first search obtains shortest routes without using an edit-matrix recurrence. Length-three input pairs check Levenshtein and full Damerau-Levenshtein, while ca -> abc distinguishes restricted adjacent swaps from the full method. Additional assertions test score range, identity and symmetry.

124/* Independent shortest-path oracle: all strings over abc up to length 4. */125static char graph[121][5];126static size_t graph_n;127/** Enumerate the finite abc spelling graph; depth four gives 1+3+9+27+81=121 nodes. */128static void strings(char *s, size_t n) {129    size_t i;130    memcpy(graph[graph_n++], s, strlen(s) + 1);131    if (n == 4) return;132    for (i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {133        s[n] = (char) ('a' + i);134        s[n + 1] = '\0';135        strings(s, n + 1);136    }137    s[n] = '\0';138}139/** Graph edge: one insertion/deletion/replacement, optionally one adjacent swap. */140static int one_edit(const char *a, const char *b, int swaps) {141    size_t n = strlen(a), m = strlen(b), i, j, d = 0;142    if (n == m) {143        size_t first = 0;144        for (i = 0; i < n; ++i) if (a[i] != b[i]) {145            if (!d) first = i;146            ++d;147        }148        if (d == 1) return 1;149        return swaps && d == 2 && first + 1 < n && a[first] == b[first + 1] && a[first + 1] == b[first] && !strcmp(a + first + 2,150            b + first + 2);151    }152    if (n > m) {153        const char *t = a;154        size_t z = n;155        a = b;156        b = t;157        n = m;158        m = z;159    }160    if (m != n + 1) return 0;161    i = 0;162    j = 0;163    while (i < n && j < m) {164        if (a[i] == b[j]) {165            ++i;166            ++j;167        } else {168            ++d;169            ++j;170        }171    }172    return d <= 1;173}174/** [PM-Or4cF6] Independent oracle: breadth-first search counts edits as graph edges.175 * It does not use the dynamic-programming recurrence being tested.176 * ca -> ac -> abc distinguishes full from restricted adjacent swaps [PM-Dl8xA4]. */177static void algorithm_tests(void) {178    size_t alg, i, j, mode;179    char tmp[5] = "";180    strings(tmp, 0);181    CHECK(graph_n == 121);182    CHECK(edit_distance("kitten", "sitting", 0) == 3);183    CHECK(edit_distance("ca", "abc", 1) == 3);184    CHECK(edit_distance("ca", "abc", 2) == 2);185    CHECK(edit_distance("ab", "ba", 0) == 2);186    CHECK(edit_distance("ab", "ba", 1) == 1);187    CHECK(edit_distance("ab", "ba", 2) == 1);188    CHECK(fabs(jaro_score("martha", "marhta") - 0.9444444444444444) < 1e-12);189    CHECK(fabs(jaro_score("dwayne", "duane") - 0.8222222222222222) < 1e-12);190    CHECK(fabs(lcs_score("abc", "ac") - 0.8) < 1e-12);191    CHECK(fabs(gram_score("abc", "abd", 1) - 0.5) < 1e-12);192    CHECK(fabs(gram_score("abcd", "abce", 0) - 1.0 / 3) < 1e-12);193    CHECK(fabs(gram_score("abcd", "abce", 2) - 0.5) < 1e-12);194    CHECK(fabs(ratcliff_score("abcd", "abxd") - 0.75) < 1e-12);195    /* These literal answers are also the calculations shown beside the code. */196    CHECK(edit_distance("ca", "cu", 0) == 1);197    CHECK(fabs(gram_score("aaaba", "aaaa", 2) - 2 / sqrt(12.0)) < 1e-12);198    CHECK(fabs(ratcliff_score("abxxcd", "abyycd") - 2.0 / 3) < 1e-12);199    {200        Prepared query;201        Property candidate;202        CHECK(prepare("request", &query));203        CHECK(property_init(&candidate, "RequestTimeout", TYPE_STRING, 0));204        CHECK(fabs(hybrid_score(&query, &candidate) - 0.5) < 1e-12);205    }206    CHECK(weighted_distance("a", "s") == 0.5);207    CHECK(weighted_distance("v1", "v2") == 2);208    CHECK(edit_distance("", "abc", 2) == 3);209    CHECK(jaro_score("", "") == 1);210    CHECK(gram_score("a", "a", 0) == 1);211    CHECK(gram_score("a", "b", 0) == 0);212    /* Breadth-first search visits paths in edit-count order. Its queue stores213     * graph indices; dist=-1 means unseen, dist=0 is the unchanged source.214     * This checks the answer without reusing the matrix recurrence under test. */215    for (mode = 0; mode < 2; ++mode) for (i = 0; i < graph_n; ++i) if (strlen(graph[i]) <= 3) {216        int dist[121], queue[121];217        size_t head = 0, tail = 1;218        for (j = 0; j < 121; ++j) dist[j] = - 1;219        dist[i] = 0;220        queue[0] = (int) i;221        while (head < tail) {222            int u = queue[head++];223            for (j = 0; j < graph_n; ++j) if (dist[j] < 0 && one_edit(graph[u], graph[j], (int) mode)) {224                dist[j] = dist[u] + 1;225                queue[tail++] = (int) j;226            }227        }228        for (j = 0; j < graph_n; ++j) if (strlen(graph[j]) <= 3) {229            double lev = edit_distance(graph[i], graph[j], 0), osa = edit_distance(graph[i], graph[j], 1), dl = edit_distance(graph[i],230                graph[j], 2);231            CHECK((mode ? dl : lev) == dist[j]);232            CHECK(dl <= osa && osa <= lev);233        }234    }235    /* Broad scorer invariants complement the known numeric answers above. */236    for (alg = 1; alg < ALGORITHMS; ++alg) for (i = 1; i < graph_n; i += 3) for (j = 1; j < graph_n; j += 4) {237        Prepared a, b;238        Property pa, pb;239        double x, y;240        CHECK(prepare(graph[i], &a));241        CHECK(prepare(graph[j], &b));242        CHECK(property_init(&pa, graph[i], TYPE_STRING, 0));243        CHECK(property_init(&pb, graph[j], TYPE_STRING, 0));244        x = algorithms[alg].score(&a, &pb);245        y = algorithms[alg].score(&b, &pa);246        CHECK(isfinite(x) && x >= - 1e-12 && x <= 1 + 1e-12);247        CHECK(fabs(x - y) < 1e-12);248        CHECK(fabs(algorithms[alg].score(&a, &pa) - 1) < 1e-12);249    }250    printf("Algorithms: independent edit-graph oracle, known answers, score ranges, identity and symmetry checked\n");251}

Test ranking and transactional configuration binding

Section titled “Test ranking and transactional configuration binding”

Reversing candidates must preserve decisions and score margins. Equal-score fuzzy candidates reject automatic assignment. Integration cases cover integer limits, booleans, duplicates, required values and rollback. A complete ten-line input checks the original configuration example.

ALGORITHMS; ++alg) {269        CHECK(registry_init(&r, "test", props, 3));270        a = resolve(&r, "catt", alg, p);271        CHECK(registry_init(&r, "test", rev, 3));272        b = resolve(&r, Exercise every nonzero byte after the standard-library change

Section titled “Exercise every nonzero byte after the standard-library change”

Literal ASCII ranges define the expected classifier behavior independently of <ctype.h>. The loop checks normalization and parser trimming for bytes 1 through 255, including values that become negative plain chars. The equals byte deliberately produces an empty-key parsing error. These checks verify the replacements rather than merely exercising their calls.

Reference for the contracts used in this file

Section titled “Reference for the contracts used in this file”

The algorithm reference guide links the definitions used by literal answer checks. The edit-graph oracle searches edit paths independently of the matrix implementation. Open reference.

502/** Check ctype integration against literal ASCII ranges, not against ctype itself. */503static void character_library_tests(void) {504    unsigned byte;505    for (byte = 1; byte <= 255; ++byte) {506        char input[] = {(char)byte, '\0'};507        char line[] = {(char)byte, 'k', '=', (char)byte, 'v', (char)byte, '\0'};508        char normalized[KEY_MAX + 1];509        Entry parsed;510        int letter_or_digit = (byte >= 'A' && byte <= 'Z') ||511                              (byte >= 'a' && byte <= 'z') || (byte >= '0' && byte <= '9');512        int whitespace = byte == ' ' || (byte >= '\t' && byte <= '\r');513        CHECK(normalize(input, normalized, sizeof normalized) == letter_or_digit);514        CHECK(parse_entry(line, &parsed) == (byte == '=' ? PARSE_EMPTY_KEY : PARSE_OK));515        CHECK(byte == '=' || (unsigned char)parsed.key[0] == (whitespace ? (unsigned char)'k' : (unsigned char)byte));516    }517}518519/** Return nonzero on any failed assertion or dataset-contract violation. */520int self_test(void) {521    static Dataset a, b;522    checks = 0;523    failures = 0;524    registries_init();525    parser_tests();526    normalization_tests();527    character_library_tests();528    algorithm_tests();529    resolver_tests();530    integration_tests();531    CHECK(load_dataset("tests/calibration_cases.csv", &a));532    CHECK(load_dataset("tests/evaluation_cases.csv", &b));533    CHECK(validate_datasets(&a, &b));534    printf("%u assertions; %u failures; calibration=%zu held-out=%zu\n", checks, failures, a.n, b.n);535    return failures ? 1 : 0;536}
